sections.h2: Fast sale options in North Tonawanda
sections.html:
Homeowners here can hire an agent, go it alone, or take a direct cash purchase, and condition plus patience usually decide. Check first that you are in the city proper. The 14120 ZIP code also reaches southern parts of the towns of Wheatfield and Pendleton.

Niagara County's second-largest city after Niagara Falls, North Tonawanda lies between the Niagara River on the west and Tonawanda Creek and the Erie Canal on the south. It has 29,806 residents, 2.3% fewer than in 2020.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $197,200
  • Share of homes lived in by owners: 70.1%
  • Median gross rent: $934 a month
  • Median household income: $66,961

Across 14,015 households of about 2.14 people, long-time owners dominate. Roughly 91% of residents stayed in the same house for a year, so listings are not constant.

sections.h2: Homes built in the Lumber City
sections.html:
Local pride runs to the nickname Lumber City, and the housing grew from that trade. From the mid-19th century into the 1970s it was a lumber forwarding center, and more than 150 lumber companies operated here. The Ray H. Bennett Lumber Company sold kit homes across the United States and Canada for about 70 years, so an older house on your block may be a kit home, a detail some buyers like to hear. Goundry Street has mansions built for lumber barons.

Location sells here too. Downtown draws buyers who like the Riviera Theatre on Webster Street, the City Market, Gateway Harbor Park on the canal, and Gratwick-Riverside Park, a 53-acre park on the Niagara River.

Under Chapter 51D of the city code, every owner of rental property in North Tonawanda registers each rental unit with the Building Department, and owner-occupied properties register too, without a fee.

North Tonawanda rental registration, yearly fee
PropertyFee
1 to 3 dwelling units$35 per unit
4 or more dwelling units$140
Owner-occupiedNo fee, registration still required

A certificate lasts up to one year or until ownership changes, which means a rental's new owner registers separately once the deed transfers. Registering consents to inspection by Code Enforcement for compliance with the city chapter and the New York State building and fire codes.

  • Applicants submit photo identification.
  • An owner who does not live in Niagara County, Erie, Genesee or Orleans County must name a property manager who does, and who can accept legal notices.
  • A first conviction for failing to register carries a fine of $250 to $500. A second within twelve months carries $500 to $2,500.
  • A fine unpaid after 30 days becomes a lien on the property and is collected like a tax.

A rental owner who sells without a current registration invites trouble, so landlords should fix any registration gap before selling, because a lien shows up in a title search. Visit the Building Department at 216 Payne Avenue or call (716) 692-2680.

Every year Grievance Day falls on the fourth Tuesday in May, and forms are at the Assessor's office from March. Use the online property search to open any parcel, choose Additional Info, then View Tax Detail, for a year by year tax summary.

Buyers ask about exemptions, so keep these basics handy:

  • Basic STAR requires owning and living in the home with income of $500,000 or less.
  • Enhanced STAR requires age 65 and adjusted gross income of $110,750 or less.
  • People who bought after 2015 sign up with the state for the STAR Credit.
  • The low-income senior exemption has an income limit of $34,400, and the disability exemption has a limit of $34,600.
  • Military service exemptions are capped for assessments above $120,000.

A free copy of your deed is available from the Assessor on request, handy when you assemble closing papers. Details at 695-8597.

sections.h2: Deeds, transfer tax and city water
sections.html:
North Tonawanda deeds are recorded by the Niagara County Clerk and not at City Hall. Call the recording office at (716) 439-7022; it is open weekdays from 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

Filing takes a signed original deed, a TP-584 transfer tax return and an RP-5217 real property transfer report. The seller pays the state transfer tax of $2 for each $500, or $4 per $1,000, due within 15 days after the deed is delivered. A closing attorney or title company normally handles this for you.

Before closing, settle city water. After two consecutive estimated water meter readings, a $25 fee applies each quarter until the meter is read, and readings can be dropped off or submitted online. Ask the Treasurer's office at (716) 695-8575 for the current balance and how it is handled at transfer.

One city school district covers North Tonawanda, and the average commute is 20.4 minutes, short enough to put in the listing. Precipitation falls on about 171 days a year and snow on about 57, so roof, gutter and basement condition deserve a close look before you list.

sections.h2: What buyers ask about a North Tonawanda house
sections.html: Buyers tend to raise the same four topics. First, age and condition: with snow on about 57 days a year, buyers look hard at roofs, gutters and basements. Second, any rental history and whether the registration is current. Third, the water meter and whether a balance is open. Fourth, which exemptions the house now carries, since a buyer must apply for their own. Written answers shorten negotiations. Direct buyers usually ask fewer questions, though a clean file still helps your price. If you sell as-is, say so in the first conversation, list the known problems, and let the offer reflect them. That keeps the number from changing after an inspection.

Give yourself a few weeks of lead time. Assemble the deed, your latest tax and water statements and a lender payoff letter, in one folder so that nothing is hunted for later. If the house is a rental, confirm the registration with the Building Department first. Your attorney can name the forms the sale needs, and the Assessor will hand over the deed copy at no charge. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, which spares you showings and repair credits, and closing follows your own calendar once the title work is done.

Ask the Treasurer for the water balance a few days before closing so no surprise reaches the table. At the closing you sign the deed and the transfer tax forms, the mortgage is paid, and the clerk records the deed. If you were a landlord, remember that the buyer registers the units in their own name afterward.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house in North Tonawanda if it is not registered?
faqs.a: Register it before the sale. Failing to register is a violation with fines of $250 to $500 for a first conviction, and an unpaid fine becomes a lien on the property.

faqs.q: Where do I file a deed after selling in North Tonawanda?
faqs.a: File it with the Niagara County Clerk. The seller pays transfer tax of $2 per $500, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms go in with the deed.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in North Tonawanda?
faqs.a: It is always the fourth Tuesday in May. Grievance forms are available from the Assessor's office starting in March.

faqs.q: Is a 14120 mailing address always inside North Tonawanda city limits?
faqs.a: No. The ZIP code 14120 also covers southern parts of the towns of Wheatfield and Pendleton, so check your tax bill to see which municipality governs your house.

faqs.q: What happens to my rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: The certificate lasts up to one year or until ownership changes. After the sale the new owner registers the units with the Building Department.
